The Power Automate server/mcp.mjs and generate-native-extension/SKILL.md are
byte-identical to acc83f5. The native skill describes generating local Kotlin,
Objective-C, React Native dispatch contracts and build metadata from a PRD.

Decisive execution-path evidence:
plugins/process-intelligence/tests/http-auth.test.mjs:48 builds a 33,000-byte
Bearer claims attribute. Lines 53-56 inject it into a synthetic 401 Response's
WWW-Authenticate header through an injected fetch function. It is not an
Authorization token sent to a server. The assertions require one token
acquisition, one synthetic request, body cancellation, CLAIMS_LOGIN_REQUIRED,
and no private payload in the error. In src/http-auth.mjs, the wrapper validates
an exact configured HTTPS endpoint before acquiring a token, sets the outgoing
Authorization header from that token, rejects redirects, and cancels a 401
response body. A claims challenge immediately throws CLAIMS_LOGIN_REQUIRED;
it does not decode or forward the challenge. Only a plain 401 can retry once.
No F5 endpoint, overflow delivery, control-flow redirection or crash hook is
present on this path.

configuration.mjs derives the endpoint from an environment GUID and fixed cloud
suffixes. authentication.mjs obtains the selected user's token from Azure CLI,
checks tenant/account/audience and expiration, and retains the token in RAM.
process.mjs launches an argv-based process with shell:false and bounded output
and cleanup; Windows .cmd launch arguments are constrained. These are expected
operations for the Process Mining MCP bridge.

Other flagged bundles:
Power Automate's esbuild wrappers contain MSAL authentication, MCP SDK, schema
validators, flow API operations, browser consent launch and registered stdio
MCP tools. Its dynamic Function construction is schema-validator compilation.
Its detached child runs the packaged telemetry dispatcher. That dispatcher
filters event fields to an explicit schema before sending collector events;
API bodies and credentials are not generic event fields. The model-apps/PCF
cds-maker-sdk.cjs bundles are byte-identical to each other and agree with their
recorded SHA256 b8497fbc98f732df23b83d4002818612a9f41c1b94bff7bbeefc5cc60e910f36.
Their emailBody matches are control/localization schema identifiers. Escaped
source regions and Unicode-decoded layers contain generated validation,
compilation, UI and SDK text. Minification and Unicode escapes do not establish
an obfuscated executable payload. The apparent reversed client distribution
path is ordinary @azure/msal-common/dist/client/AuthorizationCodeClient.mjs.
normalizeIdentity trims and lowercases account/tenant strings for consistency
checks; it does not harvest browser identities.
